subject: Next steps: SDK onboarding & 429 mitigation plan for Finovo embeddings
messages:
From: Connor O'Brien <connor@redwood.com>
To: Samir Patel <samir@finovo.com>, Anya Li <anya@finovo.com>
Cc: lauren_bishop@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 14 Oct 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Next steps: SDK onboarding & 429 mitigation plan for Finovo embeddings

Hi Samir / Anya —

Thanks again for a productive call this morning. Quick recap + proposed next steps so we have a single source of truth. High level: Finovo will ingest customer documents, compute embeddings for search/rerank, and run batched reranker calls. You expect heavy bursty traffic during nightly syncs (spikes to ~800 qps for ~5 minutes) and a steady stream of ~60 qps during business hours.

Key technical constraints we discussed:
- Security: all outbound calls must come from a static IP range and integrate with your proxy.
- Latency SLO for reranker: 200–300ms p50; embedding generation can be slightly higher.
- Data retention: embeddings stored in Finovo-managed DB; we must not log raw text.

Primary follow-ups I outlined:
1) SDK + auth: we will provide a sample SDK snippet for streaming/batch embeddings with built-in retry, request-id propagation, and a default token refresh workflow. (Attachment: redwood_sdk_backoff_sample.py)
2) Rate limiting & retries: recommend token-bucket throttling on client side, server-side quotas (per-customer API key), and exponential backoff with full jitter for 429s. Use x-redwood-request-id for idempotency; for embedding batches use deterministic batch-id to detect duplicates on our side.
3) Routing & fallbacks: route heavy batch jobs to a Dedicated pool in us-west (lower cost, higher throughput). Configure automatic fallback to a smaller hosted instance when Dedicated capacity is exhausted.
4) Structured output/tool-calling: reranker will call your internal rerank service; we tested structured JSON responses + tool-calling hooks to prevent model hallucination.

Requested from Finovo:
- A 72-hour sample QPS profile (CSV) showing hourly distribution so we can size the Dedicated pool and quota windows.
- Confirmation of the static egress IPs or proxy details.

Proposed short timeline:
- Today: Finovo shares QPS CSV and proxy IPs.
- +2 business days: Redwood provides SDK snippet, a config file for client-side throttling, and a draft routing policy.
- +1 week: PoC run (1 week), then revisit capacity sizing.

Action owners: Connor (PoC coordination), Lauren (solution architecture + quotas), Marissa (pricing/commit proposal).

If that matches your expectation, reply with the QPS CSV and any security checklist items. We can schedule a 30-min technical setup session as needed.

Thanks,
Connor O'Brien
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
connor@redwood.com
(Attachment: redwood_sdk_backoff_sample.py)
From: Samir Patel <samir@finovo.com>
To: Connor O'Brien <connor@redwood.com>
Cc: Anya Li <anya@finovo.com>
Date: Wed, 14 Oct 2026 11:08:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Next steps: SDK onboarding & 429 mitigation plan for Finovo embeddings

Connor —

Thanks for the clear recap. That aligns with Finovo's needs. A few clarifications and items from our side:
- QPS profile: attaching a short sample (finovo_qps_profile.csv) — you should see the nightly bursts and the weekday steady-state.
- Static egress: we put the calls through our proxy at proxy.finovo.com (10.45.3.12) behind an allowlist; please confirm the Redwood egress IPs or give us a CIDR.
- Idempotency: we like the deterministic batch-id idea. For embedding pipelines we tend to retry the same batch until we see an idempotent ack; so please document the TTL for any dedup cache you keep.
- Failure semantics: for reranker calls, we prefer fast fail (return 5xx to caller) rather than queueing on our side; we'll orchestrate retries from the client.

Two asks before the PoC:
1) can you share a minimal SDK snippet that shows how to set request IDs, backoff, and conditional batching?
2) what are the default server-side quota windows you enforce (per-minute, per-hour)? We need to mirror limits in our throttling proxy.

Samir
Head of Engineering — Finovo
samir@finovo.com
(Attachment: finovo_qps_profile.csv)
From: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
To: Samir Patel <samir@finovo.com>, Connor O'Brien <connor@redwood.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 14 Oct 2026 13:47:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Next steps: SDK onboarding & 429 mitigation plan for Finovo embeddings

Samir / Connor —

Thanks for the CSV, Samir. A few concrete answers and a small ask from Redwood infra:

Answers
- Server-side quota windows: by default we enforce 1-minute and 1-hour token-based quotas (configurable). Typical defaults we propose for PoC: 3,000 tokens/min and 100,000 tokens/hour per API key (we can make these per-customer). For embeddings we often express quotas as requests/minute for a given batch size — we will map that once we see your typical batch sizes.
- Dedup TTL: we keep batch dedup entries for 24 hours by default; can be adjusted per contract.
- Egress IPs/CIDR: sending a list of Redwood egress CIDRs for PoC (will follow in a separate secure doc).

What we'll provide by EOD:
- A minimal SDK snippet that wires auth, sets x-redwood-request-id, does exponential backoff with full jitter, and shows deterministic batch-id generation (attached: redwood_sdk_backoff_sample.py).
- A sample routing policy: send batch requests (batch_size >= 32) to Dedicated us-west; fallback to hosted for small batches / intermittent bursts.

Small ask: please confirm whether Finovo's proxy supports preserving incoming headers (x-request-id). If headers are dropped, we'll need another mechanism for idempotency (e.g., a signed batch token).

I'll loop Marissa for the commercial side once PoC sizing is set.

Thanks —
Lauren Bishop
Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference
lauren_bishop@redwood.com
From: Connor O'Brien <connor@redwood.com>
To: Samir Patel <samir@finovo.com>, Anya Li <anya@finovo.com>
Cc: lauren_bishop@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 15 Oct 2026 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Next steps: SDK onboarding & 429 mitigation plan for Finovo embeddings

Samir / Anya —

Consolidating the plan and owners after Lauren's notes so we can kick the PoC tomorrow if you approve:

PoC scope (7 days):
- Objective: run nightly syncs through Redwood, validate throughput, 429 behavior, and end-to-end latencies for embeddings -> reranker.
- Environment: Dedicated us-west pool for batches, hosted fallback.
- Metrics to capture: p50/p95 latency for embeddings and reranker, 429 rate, retry success rate, token consumption, and request-id dedup rate.

Deliverables & owners:
- Redwood: SDK snippet + quickstart README (Connor) — ETA: today (attached snippet).
- Redwood: routing policy + quota defaults for PoC (Lauren) — ETA: today.
- Finovo: confirm proxy header preservation + sign NDA if required for IP list (Samir) — ETA: today.
- Joint: schedule 60-min kick-off to walk PoC steps (I'll set calendar once Finovo confirms availability).

Notes on 429 handling (technical):
- Client-side: implement token-bucket for steady-state smoothing; on 429 run exponential backoff with full jitter and preserve request-id for retry deduping. For deterministic embedding batches include a sha256-based batch-id in the payload.
- Server-side: we will surface both per-minute and per-hour quota feedback via response headers (x-rw-quota-remaining, x-rw-quota-reset). When quotas are hit we respond 429 with a Retry-After and the canonical downstream idempotency key if available.
- Canary strategy: start PoC with 10% traffic to Redwood Dedicated (canary) for first 24 hours, expand as we validate metrics.

Attaching: arch_diagram_finovo_placement.pdf and the SDK snippet (redwood_sdk_backoff_sample.py). Tickets/links: HubSpot deal: https://app.hubspot.com/deals/FIN-2026-0423, Jira INF-7892 for infra work.

If this looks good, Samir please reply +1 and we will send calendar invites.

Cheers,
Connor O'Brien
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
connor@redwood.com
(Attachments: arch_diagram_finovo_placement.pdf, redwood_sdk_backoff_sample.py)
